outputs.L2:
A cooling system for molds used with metals or metal alloys includes one or more primary conduits (6), each configured to carry a main stream of cooling carrier fluid made up of compressed air and atomized water. Multiple branch conduits (7) extend from and are connected to each primary conduit (6), and each branch conduit has a second transport cross-section (S2) that is smaller than the first transport cross-section (S1) of the associated primary conduit (6).  

Each branch conduit (7) has a free end (70) designed to be inserted into a respective channel (5′) of a duct (5) formed in one of the mold half-sections (2A, 2B) of the mold (2). The primary conduit (6) includes at least one shaped, closed end portion (60) arranged to divide the cooling carrier fluid into substantially uniform secondary streams for the branch conduits (7) extending radially from it, so that these streams are delivered through the free ends (70) into the corresponding channels (5′) of each mold half-section (2A, 2B).
outputs.L3:
The system is designed to cool metal or metal alloy molds by means of a cooling carrier fluid composed of compressed air and nebulized water. This fluid is supplied to the mold in a controlled manner in order to remove heat efficiently from selected regions of the mold during operation.

The system comprises one or more main conduits configured to transport a main flow of the cooling carrier fluid. Each main conduit acts as a primary distribution line, conveying the fluid toward the areas of the mold that require cooling.

A plurality of secondary conduits branch off from each main conduit. These secondary conduits have smaller transport sections than the corresponding main conduit and are arranged to divide the main flow into multiple secondary flows. In this way, the cooling carrier fluid can be delivered to several cooling points or zones of the mold.

Each secondary conduit has a free end adapted to be inserted into a corresponding channel formed in a duct of a mold half. When inserted, the free end directs the secondary flow of cooling carrier fluid into the associated channel, allowing localized cooling of the mold material surrounding that channel.

Each main conduit further includes a shaped, closed terminal portion. This terminal portion is configured to promote distribution of the cooling carrier fluid into the secondary conduits branching from the main conduit. In particular, the shape of the closed terminal portion helps generate substantially equal secondary flows through the respective secondary conduits, thereby improving uniformity of cooling across the different regions of the mold.
outputs.L4:
A mold-cooling system for casting metals or metal alloys is provided to improve the uniformity and efficiency of cooling during molding operations. The system is designed for use with molds formed by two half-molds, each of which includes a plurality of cooling channels arranged in the regions where controlled heat removal is required.

The cooling system comprises main supply conduits configured to deliver a cooling fluid made up of compressed air and nebulized water. The compressed air acts as a carrier fluid, while the nebulized water provides an effective cooling medium capable of absorbing heat from the mold surfaces and internal mold structure. From the main conduits, the cooling fluid is directed toward a plurality of secondary conduits positioned in correspondence with the cooling channels of the mold halves.

Each secondary conduit includes a lower portion adapted to be inserted into a respective cooling channel formed in a half-mold. In this way, the cooling fluid can be introduced directly into the interior cooling passages of the mold, allowing heat to be removed from selected areas in a controlled and repeatable manner. The arrangement of multiple secondary conduits makes it possible to cool different zones of each half-mold simultaneously.

The system further includes a shaped closed terminal portion connected to the main conduits and arranged upstream of the secondary conduits. This terminal portion is configured to distribute the incoming cooling fluid among the secondary conduits in a substantially balanced manner. By shaping and closing the terminal portion appropriately, pressure and flow variations are reduced, so that each secondary conduit receives a substantially equal amount of compressed air and nebulized water.

As a result, the injection of cooling fluid into the cooling channels is more uniform across the entire mold half. This reduces localized overheating, minimizes thermal gradients, and promotes more consistent solidification of the metal or metal alloy being cast. The improved distribution of the cooling fluid also helps enhance the dimensional quality of the cast article, reduce defects caused by uneven cooling, and increase the operating efficiency and service life of the mold.

Overall, the system provides a simple and effective solution for supplying a balanced cooling flow to multiple mold-cooling channels. The combination of main conduits, inserted secondary conduits, and a shaped closed distribution terminal enables reliable and substantially uniform cooling of each half-mold during metal or metal-alloy casting operations.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for a mold cooling system using compressed air and nebulized water, with main conduits feeding radial secondary conduits inserted into channels in half-molds.
counterfactuals.output: A mold cooling system is disclosed for cooling half-molds in a molding apparatus. The system includes at least one main conduit configured to convey compressed air and nebulized water, and a plurality of secondary conduits extending radially from the main conduit. The secondary conduits are insertable into corresponding cooling channels formed in respective half-molds so as to deliver a cooling mixture along internal regions of the half-molds. In operation, compressed air entrains nebulized water through the main conduit and distributes the mixture through the radial secondary conduits into the mold channels, promoting heat removal from the half-molds by convective flow and evaporation of the nebulized water. The arrangement enables localized and substantially uniform cooling of the half-molds, reduces cooling cycle time, and may be adapted to molds having different channel geometries by selecting the number, spacing, and orientation of the secondary conduits.
counterfactuals.label: cf_1

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a single-paragraph technical description of an invention for cooling metal casting molds, including numbered elements such as main conduit (6), secondary conduits (7), half-molds (2A, 2B), and channels (5′).
counterfactuals.output: The invention relates to a cooling system for metal casting molds comprising two cooperating half-molds (2A, 2B) defining a mold cavity and provided with internal cooling channels (5′) arranged in proximity to heat-affected regions of the mold; a main conduit (6) is configured to receive and distribute a cooling fluid, such as water, oil, air, or a pressurized gas mixture, and is fluidically connected to a plurality of secondary conduits (7) extending toward respective channels (5′) in the half-molds (2A, 2B), each secondary conduit (7) being dimensioned and positioned to deliver a controlled flow of cooling fluid to selected zones of the mold so as to promote uniform heat extraction during and after casting. The main conduit (6) may be arranged externally or partially integrated within the mold structure, while the secondary conduits (7) may include valves, flow restrictors, quick-coupling fittings, or thermal control devices to independently regulate cooling of the half-molds (2A, 2B). The channels (5′) may be formed by drilling, milling, additive manufacturing, or insertion of tubular elements, and may follow straight, curved, or conformal paths to optimize thermal exchange, reduce solidification defects, shorten cycle time, and limit thermal stress and deformation of the mold components.
counterfactuals.label: cf_2

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate claim-like language for a system that cools molds for metals or metal alloys by distributing substantially equal flows of an air-water cooling carrier fluid from a closed shaped terminal portion into multiple secondary conduits.
counterfactuals.output:
1. A system for cooling a mold for casting metals or metal alloys, the system comprising:  
   a source of an air-water cooling carrier fluid;  
   a primary conduit in fluid communication with the source;  
   a distribution body coupled to the primary conduit, the distribution body including a closed shaped terminal portion configured to receive the air-water cooling carrier fluid; and  
   a plurality of secondary conduits extending from the distribution body and configured to deliver the air-water cooling carrier fluid to respective cooling regions of the mold,  
   wherein the closed shaped terminal portion is configured to distribute substantially equal flows of the air-water cooling carrier fluid into the plurality of secondary conduits.

2. The system of claim 1, wherein the closed shaped terminal portion comprises a generally annular, arcuate, domed, bulbous, or manifold-shaped chamber.

3. The system of claim 1, wherein each of the plurality of secondary conduits has substantially the same flow resistance.

4. The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of secondary conduits are arranged symmetrically about the closed shaped terminal portion.

5. The system of claim 1, wherein the closed shaped terminal portion is free of a through-flow outlet downstream of the plurality of secondary conduits.

6. The system of claim 1, wherein the air-water cooling carrier fluid comprises a mixture of compressed air and atomized or entrained water.

7. The system of claim 1, wherein the mold comprises a continuous casting mold, an ingot mold, a die-casting mold, or a mold for casting steel, aluminum, copper, or an alloy thereof.

8. The system of claim 1, wherein the plurality of secondary conduits are configured to discharge the air-water cooling carrier fluid onto or into cooling passages associated with the mold.

9. The system of claim 1, further comprising a flow-conditioning element disposed upstream of the closed shaped terminal portion.

10. The system of claim 1, wherein the closed shaped terminal portion defines an internal volume selected to reduce velocity imbalance in the air-water cooling carrier fluid before the fluid enters the plurality of secondary conduits.

11. The system of claim 1, wherein outlets of the plurality of secondary conduits are positioned at substantially equal radial or axial spacing relative to the mold.

12. The system of claim 1, wherein the system is configured such that a flow rate through each secondary conduit differs from an average flow rate through the plurality of secondary conduits by no more than about 10 percent.

13. The system of claim 1, wherein the closed shaped terminal portion is configured to inhibit preferential flow into any one of the plurality of secondary conduits.

14. The system of claim 1, wherein the distribution body is removably coupled to the primary conduit.

15. A method of cooling a mold for metals or metal alloys, the method comprising:  
   supplying an air-water cooling carrier fluid through a primary conduit to a closed shaped terminal portion of a distribution body;  
   distributing the air-water cooling carrier fluid from the closed shaped terminal portion into a plurality of secondary conduits at substantially equal flow rates; and  
   delivering the air-water cooling carrier fluid through the plurality of secondary conduits to respective cooling regions of the mold.

16. The method of claim 15, wherein distributing the air-water cooling carrier fluid comprises equalizing pressure within the closed shaped terminal portion before the air-water cooling carrier fluid enters the plurality of secondary conduits.

17. The method of claim 15, wherein the air-water cooling carrier fluid is delivered as a two-phase mixture of air and water.

18. The method of claim 15, wherein the mold is used to cast a molten metal or metal alloy.

19. A cooling manifold for a metal casting mold, comprising:  
   an inlet configured to receive an air-water cooling carrier fluid;  
   a closed shaped terminal chamber in fluid communication with the inlet; and  
   a plurality of outlet conduits in fluid communication with the closed shaped terminal chamber,  
   wherein the closed shaped terminal chamber is shaped and dimensioned to divide the air-water cooling carrier fluid among the plurality of outlet conduits in substantially equal portions for cooling the metal casting mold.

counterfactuals.output:
A possible European patent-style formulation is:

**Patent wording**

The apparatus comprises at least one main conduit configured for conveying a flow of compressed air containing nebulized water. A plurality of secondary conduits branch from the main conduit, each secondary conduit extending downwardly from a region located below the main conduit. Each secondary conduit has a free end portion adapted to be received in a corresponding duct formed in a mold half, so as to deliver the flow of compressed air and nebulized water into said duct.

The main conduit further comprises a terminal portion arranged downstream of the secondary conduits, the terminal portion being configured to promote balancing of the flow distribution between the secondary conduits.

**Possible claim wording**

1. An apparatus for supplying nebulized water to a mold, comprising:  
   at least one main conduit configured to transport compressed air carrying nebulized water;  
   a plurality of secondary conduits branching from the main conduit at positions located below the main conduit;  
   wherein each secondary conduit comprises a free end configured to be inserted into a respective duct provided in a mold half; and  
   wherein the main conduit comprises a terminal portion configured to balance distribution of the compressed air carrying nebulized water among the secondary conduits.

2. The apparatus according to claim 1, wherein the secondary conduits extend substantially downwardly from the main conduit.

3. The apparatus according to claim 1 or 2, wherein the terminal portion is arranged downstream of the plurality of secondary conduits with respect to the direction of flow through the main conduit.

4. The apparatus according to any one of the preceding claims, wherein the free ends of the secondary conduits are removably insertable into the respective ducts of the mold half.

5. The apparatus according to any one of the preceding claims, wherein the terminal portion defines a volume, restriction, or extension selected to reduce pressure differences between the secondary conduits.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe a cooling apparatus for die-casting molds in formal patent terminology, emphasizing radial secondary conduits originating from a main conduit and injecting cooling fluid into corresponding channels of each half-mold.
counterfactuals.output:
A cooling apparatus for a die-casting mold comprising first and second half-molds, the apparatus comprising:

a primary cooling conduit configured to receive a cooling fluid from a supply source; and

a plurality of secondary cooling conduits extending radially outwardly from the primary cooling conduit,

wherein each of the secondary cooling conduits is arranged in fluid communication with a respective cooling channel formed in a corresponding one of the first and second half-molds, such that cooling fluid conveyed through the primary cooling conduit is distributed through the secondary cooling conduits and injected into the respective cooling channels of the half-molds.

In one embodiment, the primary cooling conduit is disposed substantially centrally relative to the die-casting mold, and the secondary cooling conduits are angularly spaced about the primary cooling conduit to provide substantially uniform cooling fluid distribution. Each secondary cooling conduit may terminate at an outlet or injection port positioned to introduce the cooling fluid directly into an associated cooling channel of a respective half-mold. The cooling channels may be configured to direct the cooling fluid along predetermined thermal regions of the half-molds to remove heat generated during a die-casting operation.

The apparatus may further comprise sealing means disposed between the secondary cooling conduits and the respective cooling channels to inhibit leakage of the cooling fluid, and connection means for selectively coupling the primary cooling conduit to a pressurized cooling fluid source. The radial arrangement of the secondary cooling conduits provides simultaneous distribution of cooling fluid to multiple cooling channels of both half-molds, thereby improving thermal regulation and reducing cycle time during die-casting.
